newsitem.title: USA: Witnesses say sergeant's sex partners were unhappy.
newsitem.headline: Witnesses say sergeant's sex partners were unhappy.

text.p: A defence witness in the court martial of Army Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson testified Tuesday that a female trainee Simpson is accused of raping had expressed unhappiness over a sexual encounter with him.

"(Rape) wasn't actually said, but when she was talking to me about it, it wasn't a happy feeling. The way I was talking to her I had to drag out of her," said Army Spec. Hannah Pitt, who had previously told investigators the trainee and Simpson had had consensual sex.

Simpson, 32, is charged with 19 counts of rape involving six women, and with 35 other counts including indecent exposure, battery and maltreatment. He has pleaded innocent to those charges but has admitted 11 counts of improper sexual intercourse with trainees and five of propositioning.

His lawyers were expected to rest their case Tuesday. They have argued that all of Simpson's sexual encounters were consensual, and reflected an atmosphere of wanton sexual activity at the Army's Orndance Centre and School, part of the Aberdeen Proving Ground.
Simpson is the first of 12 trainers at the proving ground charged with sexual misconduct to go to trial.

Also testifying Tuesday, Pvt. Donna Jackson said the trainee Pitt had testified about had sex with Simpson more than once. But she also acknowledged, under cross-examination from prosecutor Capt. Theresa Gallagher, that the woman tried to warn others about drill sergeants at the facility.
"She was also warning you about the drill sergeants, that they did cruddy things to people?" Gallagher said.
Referring to a conversation with the woman regarding an encounter with Simpson, Jackson said, "She didn't say 'rape' to me when I spoke to her that night, but she was angry towards him (Simpson)."

E-4 Tamila Carrington, who said she had consensual sex with Simpson between May 1995 and August 1995, testified that an alleged victim was laughing about her sexual experience with Simpson. Carrington said she reunited with her Aberdeen friend a year later.
"We were laughing because it was funny," Carrington said.
Carrington said she believed that if her friend was raped, she would have told her. "She would have confided in me. She trusted me," she said.
